items.summary: Current Desktop process has CODEX_APP_SERVER_USE_LOCAL_DAEMON=1 and is attached to the daemon path.
Desktop and daemon share the same kernel socket endpoint, but bundled Desktop Codex 0.148.0-alpha.9 differs from daemon 0.146.0.
No private stdio app-server child was found in the sampled Desktop process tree.
First switch/restart requirement was not tested because production Desktop was not changed.
Transaction rollback is covered in isolated tests, but real Desktop kill/restart recovery is untested.
Codex 0.146.0 exposes codex resume --remote unix://PATH as the formal interactive attach option; full TUI smoke remains untested.
app-server proxy forwards raw WebSocket bytes and JSON-RPC; it is not a TUI protocol.
Two raw clients both received thread/started and thread/status/changed notifications.
Unsubscribe returned unsubscribed, but no authenticated turn notification existed to prove complete suppression.
Fresh thread/started can precede state DB materialization; immediate thread/list returned zero. Desktop sidebar remains unknown.
Persisted turn pages re-read stably after restart; complete started/delta/completed item identity was not authenticated-provider tested.
The same clientUserMessageId produced two different successful turn IDs at app-server level.
Persisted cursor survived restart, but a newly acknowledged in-progress turn was not immediately visible in history; compact was not supported by this unauthenticated probe.
thread/items/list returned -32601 unsupported at runtime despite schema presence.
Synthetic isolated catalog/normalizer/bounded-reader measurements are bounded and within local targets; real provider/network/UI latency remains unknown.
Daemon mode disables the older rollout content monitor and uses shared observer plus long cold reconcile; immediate cold-thread coverage is not proven.
No authenticated provider approval was run; Bridge exact-generation safety is tested, while independent Desktop-owned approval must fail closed.
Current v2 registry, wire, mirror, continuity, SQLite and Cubit merge/alias paths were inventoried; no deletion was performed.
No automated test currently proves real Bridge WSS through Dart decoder, SQLite, Repository, Cubit and rendered semantic receipt.
Current Mobile source restores unconfirmed pending submissions as failed and only explicit retry dispatches them; physical-device version is unknown.
The checked-in protocol fixture provenance records an older Bridge head, so it is not current-HEAD proof.
